question: Eisenmenger syndrome refers to the reversal of a left-to-right intracardiac shunt to right-to-left shunting due to progressive pulmonary arterial hypertension, making the underlying defect inoperable.

l10n.wrongAnswerMessage: This statement is TRUE. Eisenmenger syndrome describes the progression from a large L-R shunt (VSD/ASD/PDA) through pulmonary vascular obstructive disease to R-L shunt reversal with cyanosis. Once established, it renders the lesion inoperable. Early surgical closure before pulmonary vascular resistance rises irreversibly is critical.
l10n.correctAnswerMessage: Correct. Eisenmenger syndrome is the endpoint of uncorrected large L-R shunts: sustained pulmonary overcirculation → obliterative pulmonary vascular disease → pulmonary artery pressures exceed systemic → shunt reversal to R-L → cyanosis. At this stage, surgical correction would offload the right ventricle into a non-functioning pulmonary circuit and is contraindicated.
